notes.body: The root أ-م-ن (a-ma-na) means to be safe, secure, or to believe. From this root, we get إِيمَان (īmān), which means faith or belief, as in the phrase أَهْلُ الْإِيمَانِ (ahl al-īmān), 'people of faith.' Another derivative is أَمِين (amīn), meaning trustworthy or safe, as in اَلْأَمِينُ الْمُخْلِصُ (al-amīn al-mukhlis), 'the loyal and trustworthy one.' We also have أَمْن (amn), meaning security or safety, as in اَلْأَمْنُ وَالسَّلَامُ (al-amnu wa-s-salāmu), 'security and peace.' In this chapter, when we speak of 'believers' approaching the Master, it highlights that their entry into this 'conversation made of doors' is not just about acquiring information, but about a foundational state of trust and security that allows for true learning and transformation.

The word for 'knowledge' in Arabic is عِلْم (ʿilm). It comes from the root ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m), which means 'to know' or 'to learn.' From this root, we get words like عَالِم (ʿālim), meaning 'a knower' or 'scholar,' as in هُوَ عَالِمٌ كَبِيرٌ (He is a great scholar). We also have مَعْلُوم (maʿlūm), meaning 'known' or 'information,' as in هَذِهِ مَعْلُومَةٌ مُهِمَّةٌ (This is important information). And تَعْلِيم (taʿlīm) means 'teaching' or 'instruction,' as in تَعْلِيمُ الْأَطْفَالِ (the teaching of children). This chapter emphasizes that true knowledge (عِلْم) isn't just passively received; it's actively sought and often revealed through the 'doors' of inquiry and conversation, aligning with the root's sense of active learning.

The word مَوْلَى comes from the root و-ل-ي (wa-la-ya), which means to be near, to be a friend, or to be a protector. From this root, we get words like وَلِيّ (walīy), meaning a friend, guardian, or even a saint, as in أَوْلِيَاء الله (awliyāʾ Allāh), 'friends of God'. Another derivative is وِلَايَة (wilāyah), which signifies guardianship or authority. In this chapter, the 'Master' (مَوْلَى) is not just a teacher but a spiritual guide and protector, someone who has authority and closeness to the divine, opening doors of understanding for the disciple.
